                                          The Commission’s Routing Criteria

         Applying the Commission’s routing criteria, Route 891 and Staff’s Alternative Route 296

emerge as the best choices. The Commission’s authority and obligation to evaluate transmission

line routes is governed by both statute and Commission rules. Public Utility Regulatory Act

(“PURA”) § 37.056(c)(4) and Commission Rule § 25.101(b)(3)(B) require the Commission to

approve or deny a CCN application only after considering, among other factors: whether a

proposed route parallels or utilizes existing compatible ROW, public roads, or property lines;

environmental integrity; costs to consumers; and, the policy of prudent avoidance.24 Route 891

and Staff’s Alternative Route 296 parallel a greater proportion of property boundaries, compatible

ROW, and existing roads than the Applicants’ Proposed Route.

         The Commission’s routing criteria for paralleling property lines and compatible ROW are

a substantive obligation that reflect a deliberate policy judgment: the necessary taking of land for

a transmission line should be done in the least intrusive manner possible, particularly by following

the edges of landowners’ property rather than cutting through their interior.25

                     b.    Opposition to Link G13

        Link G13 and G51 cross the Mill Creek and Rocky Creek tributaries near their confluence

with the Lampasas River, which watershed has been formally recognized as ecologically

significant and vulnerable to exactly the kinds of land disturbance associated with a major

transmission corridor.57 The Texas A&M University System has developed and implemented the

Lampasas River Watershed Protection Plan (the “WPP”) in collaboration with local stakeholders,

Environmental Quality’s Nonpoint Source Management Program, which Plan would be directly

threatened by paralleling lengths of the river and crossing particularly sensitive tributaries.58 For

example, the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department has further designated the Rocky Creek
